Even with almost no shrinkage the NE-rate readout reaches only R² 0.62. It still mostly encodes whether NE is on: about 0.33 at rate 0.05 and only 0.71 at 1.0, with a scatter of about 0.15. Halving a 1.0 rate would move it by roughly 0.1. Turning that into a −2.4 mmHg response would take a gain near 20, which adds about 3 mmHg of noise to MAP predictions. So norepinephrine is out of reach for a value-head edit, and NE stays unedited.

The insulin edit at −2.6 was only checked against truth on one tuning batch (f3: −13.01 against −13.18, and +5.41 against +6.59). Before finishing, I will run the dose_edit rollout on a different batch, tu1 (2020000200..299), and compare it with my record-based truth for those stays. A model-to-truth ratio near 0.95–1.0 for x2, and about 0.8 for x1/2, would confirm the calibration carries over to other stays. A clearly different ratio would mean the gain is fitted to f3.
